classification.difficultyReason: Combine equal tangents, an isosceles right triangle and the radius–tangent relationship to prove an angle bisector.

content.prompt: $AD$ is the diameter of a circle $ADB$, with centre $O$. $BC$ is the tangent to the circle at $B$, $AC\perp BC$ and $AC$ is tangent to the circle at $A$. Prove that $BA$ bisects $\angle CAD$.

spec.description: Unshaded circle with horizontal diameter AD, centre O, upper tangent CB extended to the right, vertical tangent CA and a right-angle marker at C. BA is intentionally absent from the question diagram. Decorative blue strokes and the red centre marker are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: A and D are opposite ends of a diameter. B is the upper point of tangency. CA and CB meet perpendicularly at C.
spec.answerVisibility: No angle values or proof construction are supplied.

answer.short:
$\angle CAB=\angle BAD=45^\circ$, so $BA$ bisects $\angle CAD$.

Use equal tangents from $C$ and the perpendicular radius and tangent at $A$.
answer.worked:
Join $A$ to $B$. Since tangents from the same external point are equal, $CA=CB$. Thus $\triangle CAB$ is isosceles. Also $\angle ACB=90^\circ$ because $AC\perp BC$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle CAB=\angle CBA&=\frac{180^\circ-90^\circ}{2}\\\angle CAB=\angle CBA&=45^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The tangent $AC$ is perpendicular to radius $OA$. Since $A$, $O$ and $D$ are collinear, $\angle CAD=90^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle BAD&=90^\circ-45^\circ\\\angle BAD&=45^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\angle CAB=\angle BAD$, so $BA$ bisects $\angle CAD$.
